newsitem.title: HONG KONG: More HK people happy as handover day looms --poll.
newsitem.headline: More HK people happy as handover day looms --poll.

text.p: More Hong Kong people are happy about their imminent return to Chinese rule and most prefer to stay in the territory, according to the results of a recent survey released on Wednesday.

The poll, conducted by the Social Sciences Research Centre at the University of Hong Kong on May 27, found 23.8 percent of respondents were optimistic and happy about the handover, up from 21 percent in the similar poll in mid-May.

Hong Kong, a British colony of 156 years, reverts to Chinese rule in just 13 days on July 1. Pulse-taking exercises such as opinion polls have become a familiar feature in the territory in the run-up to the historic changeover.
The latest survey, which polled 531 people, found 13.4 percent of respondents feeling negative or anxious about the handover, up from 11.2 percent in mid-May.
However, 78.7 percent of those polled said they would prefer to stay in Hong Kong, up from 72.1 percent.
Some 15.9 percent said they would leave if they could, down from 16.9 percent in mid-May.
But perhaps the most resounding vote of confidence came when respondents were asked where they would invest money for the long term.
Some 55.2 percent said they would invest it in Hong Kong, the highest level since at least the end of 1996.
The university also found that confidence levels have been rising steadily since its programme started in 1994.

So far in 1997, an average of 71.2 percent of respondents have expressed confidence in Hong Kong's future, up from 62.7 percent in 1996 and 58.1 percent in 1995. Only 56.1 percent were confident in 1994.
As for those not confident in the future, the number has fallen to an average of 11.8 percent so far in 1997, from 16.2 percent in 1996, 21.8 percent in 1995 and 21.4 percent in 1994.
